Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Wednesday for an immediate end to his long-running corruption trial after judges cast doubt on the charges and recommended dropping a case in which he is accused of bribery.

The judges’ recommendations came as Israel’s longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival following the inconclusive elections on 27 October.

articles.title: Netanyahu’s Likud formally challenges election results at 120 polling stations
articles.summary: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party formally challenged the election results late Wednesday, seeking to have voting repeated at 120 polling stations, according to media reports. The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper said Likud filed an appeal with the Jerusalem District Court, sitting as an administrative court, asking it to annul the results from 120 polling stations and order new voting at those locations. The Haaretz newspaper said the party “submitted affidavits alleging irregularities at dozens of polling stations in Arab towns, most involving the transfer of information about voters’ identities in violation of rulings by the Central Elections Committee and the Supreme Court.” “The appeal did not include evidence of electoral bribery or widespread fraud,” it said. articles.title: Oil tanker catches fire after hitting naval mine in Strait of Hormuz: Iranian Navy
articles.summary: An oil tanker caught fire and was left immobilized Wednesday after striking a naval mine in a restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Navy said, Anadolu reports. In a statement carried by the semi-official Mehr news agency, the Navy said the tanker had disabled its detection and navigation systems before entering “the prohibited area” despite receiving warnings. The vessel subsequently struck a naval mine, caught fire, and came to a standstill, the statement added. The navy did not identify the tanker or provide details about its crew, possible casualties, or the extent of the damage. The reported incident comes amid continued disruptions to maritime traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global […]

articles.title: Not in God’s name: Why Palestine’s liberation struggle is not a religious war
articles.summary: A Palestinian Christian priest, Father Issa Thaljieh, was denied a US visa in November, for seemingly no other reason than the fact that he is Palestinian. “I believe the reason for the rejection is that I’m a Palestinian and live in this Holy Land,” he said. Around the same time, the US welcomed with open arms a wanted Israeli war criminal, former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, who attended a conference in New York, despite an outstanding arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court. The contrast is striking. But to call it mere hypocrisy is to miss the deeper contradiction it exposes: the deliberate distortion of how the Middle East and its people are portrayed.  For decades, the US government, […]

archive.security_status_cs: V Gaze pokračují intenzivní střety a cílené útoky IDF na velitele Hamásu, zatímco v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu došlo k incidentu s ropným tankerem po nárazu na námořní minu. V Sýrii se mezitím objevují další útoky spojované s ISIL a diplomatické napětí mezi USA a Íránem nadále zaměstnává regionální aktéry.
archive.security_status_en: Intense clashes and targeted IDF strikes against Hamas commanders continue in Gaza, while an oil tanker incident near the Strait of Hormuz highlights growing maritime risks following a naval mine strike. Meanwhile, ISIL-linked attacks in Syria persist, and diplomatic tensions between the US and Iran continue to preoccupy regional actors.
